prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, a general method for constructing aryl amines.

statement.case_for: I keep B069 alone, with Buchwald and Hartwig. Round 1 did not weaken the case on maturity or attribution: every member who discussed it, including its critics, accepted that it has the cleanest credit and the longest record of independent confirmation on the shortlist. What the objections left open is novelty relative to 2010, and I think that has a chemical answer. The 2010 prize covered C-C coupling of organometallic partners. Amination needed different mechanistic solutions: amine binding and deprotonation at palladium, and the competing beta-hydride elimination pathway, with reductive elimination of the C-N bond as the difficult step. These were solved by deliberate ligand design, first chelating phosphines and then bulky biaryl and hindered alkyl phosphines, and tested against isolated intermediates and kinetics, as Zou notes. The result is a method that medicinal and process chemists use as a default operation, which is the clearest sign that a reaction has changed practice. Two names, no arbitrary cut.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is the one Chabes, Sparr, Aqvist and the chair raise: after the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the 2021 organocatalysis prize, a further palladium coupling prize looks like a refinement of a recognised reaction class by ligand engineering, and it adds a better route to a bond rather than a new mode of action. I cannot argue that C-N coupling is a new paradigm. Kosugi and Migita's tin-amide chemistry is a real precursor and the credit story is not perfectly tidy, even if neither supplied a general catalyst. If the committee decides novelty of capability should outweigh maturity and clean credit, B045 is the stronger answer.

responses.point: Linke accepts B069 as the cleanest attribution with the best maturity profile and keeps it as first alternative, but says the ligand-design logic refines a bond construction the 2010 prize framed, whereas degradation adds a mode of action.
responses.response: I accept the distinction between a new capability and a better route, and I do not claim B069 is a new modality. But a new route to an old bond can change practice more than a new concept does when it makes a transformation routine. Aryl amines were largely made by nitration and reduction or by harsh copper chemistry before 1995, and now they are made by a Pd or Ni-catalysed step in nearly every medicinal chemistry programme. On your fallback, I take it that you could accept B069 if clean credit and maturity dominate, and that is the question I think the committee has to settle explicitly.

responses.point: Aili concedes B069 is the safer prize with a cleaner case on maturity and attribution than B045, and describes certainty over novelty as a legitimate position, while arguing degraders open a modality with wider biomedical reach.
responses.response: I accept that framing and agree it is a legitimate choice rather than a lack of ambition. I would add that your own text lists the weaknesses a B045 citation has to carry: no approved PROTAC, a PROTAC concept and a cereblon mechanism that are two different achievements, and five credible people (Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim, Ito) outside the trio. The chair asks whether Ciulli displaces Handa. I cannot see a principled answer within three names, since Handa's cereblon work and Ciulli's VHL ligands are both foundational to different parts of the field. That is why I would sooner award a prize whose boundaries are not contested. If the committee settles the allocation convincingly, my ranking of B045 would rise.

responses.point: Zou agrees on attribution and maturity, says the ligand-design logic was tested against isolated intermediates and kinetics, which separates C-N coupling from a scope expansion of 2010, and would not add Kosugi as a third laureate.
responses.response: I agree and have taken the mechanistic point into my case. It also answers Brzezinski's request to see how much rests on mechanism rather than on synthetic utility: the catalytic cycle for amination, including amine coordination, deprotonation and C-N reductive elimination, was worked out through isolated intermediates and kinetics, and that work guided the ligand generations. On the credit, I add that Kosugi and Migita showed tin amides could couple but not a general catalyst for free amines. I would not name Kosugi, and I would not use the citation to adjudicate that chronology.

responses.point: Brzezinski says the committee must be convinced that C-N coupling is distinct from 2010 and has ligand-design logic not covered by that recognition, and would let B069 rank above several of his candidates if expert reports support this, while asking how much rests on mechanism versus utility.
responses.response: I think the mechanistic content is substantial: for amination the rate-limiting steps and the side reactions differ from the C-C case, and the ligand families developed for it came from understanding them. I would not claim this is mechanism alone, since utility in synthesis is the reason it has lasted. On your B006, I stay unconvinced that it is distinct enough from Marcus theory, because the tunnelling-pathway picture involves Beratan, Onuchic and Dutton, and a Gray and Winkler pairing would leave them out. I would not support it over B069.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat C-N coupling as distinct enough from the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the 2021 organocatalysis prize, or as a further refinement of a recognised area.
Priority between Kosugi and Migita and Buchwald and Hartwig in 1994-1995; I believe the question concerns generality, not the first observation.
Whether the committee can find a defensible B045 trio, and whether a degrader prize without an approved PROTAC drug is mature enough.
I considered a two-part configuration, but any second part would have to be a single name from B045, B054 or B026 and I cannot make that cut non-arbitrary, so I keep a single part.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no personal or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi or any other credited candidate. As a synthetic organic chemist I am professionally close to the field of B069, which I have tried to offset by arguing from the mechanistic and attribution record, not from familiarity.
